key_insight: Coding agents can design non-neural controllers that reach RL returns, but success is inconsistent and return alone does not establish robustness.
engineering_relevance: ControlHarbor evaluates executable controllers against ordered requirements, physical perturbations and structural certificates, making it relevant to specification-driven control engineering.
method: Formulate controller design as a chance-constrained feasibility problem.
Submit a single Python file mapping measurements to actions, without neural networks.
Evaluate on held-out seeds using shared environments for coding agents and learning algorithms.
evidence_signal: Across 44 tasks over 13 plants, three frontier coding agents reached RL returns on every parity task, but only in a minority of sessions.
watch_item: Robustness remains conditional: structured design matched RL return under the humanoid robustness specification, but only domain-randomised RL succeeded under large pushes.
paper_title: ControlHarbor: A Benchmark for Control Design by Coding Agents
